name: Black Canyon of the Colorado
agency: NPS Lake Mead National Recreation Area

camps.name: Arizona Hot Springs
camps.desc: Camping is allowed on any available beach, and a pit toilet serves the hot springs. Gold Strike and Arizona Hot Springs close mid-May to September for heat.

camps.name: Emerald Cave beaches
camps.desc: Beaches below the cave; camping is allowed on any available beach.

camps.name: Willow Beach
camps.desc: A campground with nine tent sites and a 28-site full-service RV park, with a marina, store and restaurant.

rapids.name: Ringbolt Rapid
rapids.desc: A riffle at Arizona Hot Springs, river mile 59.75.

hikes.name: Sauna Cave
hikes.desc: A 50-foot tunnel begun during dam construction, ending in a geothermal pool and natural steam room. The back requires crawling. River mile 63.

hikes.name: Nevada Hot Springs (Gold Strike)
hikes.desc: Walk up Gold Strike Canyon wash to a series of blue pools of 85 to 105 degrees. River mile 62.5. The trail has eight rope-assisted descents of about 20 feet each; kayakers can reach it from the river.

hikes.name: Boy Scout Canyon
hikes.desc: The first pools are about a quarter mile upstream; going further requires scrambling with installed ropes at small waterfalls. River mile 61.75.

hikes.name: Arizona Hot Springs
hikes.desc: Pools in a slot canyon with walls as narrow as 6 feet, reached by a metal ladder beside a warm waterfall. River mile 59.75.

hikes.name: Emerald Cave
hikes.desc: A shallow cave on the Arizona side. Glide in backwards; at the right angle sunlight makes the water sparkle green. River mile 54.5.

trail: Designated in 2014, the first National Water Trail in the Southwest and the first flowing through a desert. About 30 miles from the base of Hoover Dam to Eldorado Canyon (river mile 39), with Willow Beach in between.

The trail continues 18 miles to Eldorado Canyon, named by Spanish gold seekers. Expect open water, wind and fast current with hidden rocks. Paddlers carry watercraft about a quarter mile up a desert wash to reach a vehicle.
indigenous: The Colorado River corridor through Black Canyon lies in the homelands of the Mojave and Southern Paiute peoples, who traveled and lived along the river and in the desert uplands on either side long before the dam.
history: Black Canyon was chosen as the site for the dam authorized in 1928. Construction ran from 1931 to 1936. The 726-foot concrete arch holds back Lake Mead and sets the cold, clear flow you float on.
In 1858 the army’s Ives expedition pushed the small steamer Explorer up the Colorado as far as Black Canyon, where it struck a rock. It was an early steamboat attempt on the river above the Gulf.
The Mike O’Callaghan–Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge, opened in 2010, carries US 93 across the canyon just below the dam, about 900 feet above the water. Look up from the first mile.
geology: The canyon walls are volcanic rock, lava flows, ash and breccia from the Miocene, roughly 13 to 16 million years ago, broken by faults. Water heated deep underground rises along those fractures to feed the hot springs in Gold Strike, Boy Scout and Arizona Hot Springs canyons, which is why the side canyons run warm and steamy.
flows: Water comes from deep in Lake Mead, so the river runs clear and about 54 degrees all year. Releases change with power demand and the level can move several feet in a day, so tie up before you hike.

rules.name: Boat zones, Hoover Dam to Willow Beach

rules.d: Year-round, motorless recreation only. Personal watercraft and motorized vessels are prohibited.

rules.t: Tuesday to Saturday, Labor Day to Memorial Day weekend
rules.d: Personal watercraft are prohibited and motors are limited to 65 horsepower or less.

rules.t: Tuesday to Saturday, Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day
rules.d: No horsepower limits and personal watercraft are allowed.
Houseboating, water-skiing and wakeboarding are prohibited year-round.
Life jackets must be worn while underway.
Water below the dam is about 53 degrees year-round and levels can change 4 to 6 vertical feet during the day. Tie up your boat when exploring side canyons; a beach can flood within an hour.
Upriver winds are common and can make paddling very difficult, especially on a stand-up paddleboard.
Naegleria fowleri can be present in hot springs. Keep water out of your nose while soaking.
The canyon is remote with limited rescue options. Accompany trips south of Burro Wash with a powerboat. Check the NPS site for flash flood and side-canyon conditions.
The trail is open year-round. Spring and fall are best for the hot springs; Gold Strike and Arizona Hot Springs close from mid-May to September for extreme heat.

landmarks.name: Hoover Dam
landmarks.desc: Launch point at river mile 64. A bridge spans the tall cliffs above. Launching requires a permit through an approved vendor, who shuttles you into the Federal Security Zone; you have about 15 minutes to launch.

landmarks.name: Emerald Cave
landmarks.desc: River mile 54.5, about 2 miles upstream of Willow Beach.

landmarks.name: Gauging station
landmarks.desc: The historic station that monitored water level, flow and silt before and during Hoover Dam's construction, on the Nevada side. Two cable cars and a catwalk link it to the gauger's home.

landmarks.name: Gauger's Homesite
landmarks.desc: Where the gauger who collected Colorado River data lived from 1935 to 1939. Only the foundation and retaining walls remain.

landmarks.name: Willow Beach
landmarks.desc: River mile 52.5. Paddlecraft launch and take out here at a marina with a launch ramp, rentals, store and restaurant, and a National Fish Hatchery with self-guided tours.

notes.camp: *Camp well above the waterline: Hoover Dam releases can raise or lower the river several feet in a day. There are no designated sites; use any available beach and carry out all waste.
notes.hike: *The hot-spring hikes are steep, rope-assisted scrambles in slot canyons that can flash flood. Pools can be well over 100 degrees; soak briefly and keep water out of your nose. Gold Strike and Arizona Hot Springs close in summer heat.

access.note: Take-out. 14 miles south of the dam off US 93

permit.status: Required to launch at Hoover Dam · through approved vendors

items.d: A permit is required to launch below Hoover Dam. It is issued through a limited number of approved vendors, who also provide the shuttle into the Federal Security Zone. You cannot self-shuttle.
Dates can sell out months ahead, particularly in spring and fall.
The launch is inside a security zone, so you have about 15 minutes to rig and go.
Paddlecraft can launch and take out at Willow Beach and paddle upstream. No dam launch permit is needed; a park entrance fee applies.
Camping is allowed on any available beach. Carry a portable toilet; the only pit toilet is at Arizona Hot Springs.
